vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: shlibrary-seat-booking
Version: 0.1.6

The skill is a legitimate automation tool for booking seats at the Shanghai Library East Branch. It uses Playwright (scripts/login_and_get_auth_node.js) to facilitate a manual user login and capture session tokens (accessToken, sign, timestamp), which are stored locally in the user's home directory (~/.config/shlibrary-seat-booking/) with restricted permissions (0o600). The code is well-documented, includes comprehensive unit tests, and interacts exclusively with official library domains (library.sh.cn) without any evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill's code, install steps, and runtime instructions are consistent with a browser-assisted seat-booking CLI: it requires Node/Playwright, reads/writes local profile files for library auth, and talks only to the library booking endpoints documented in the repository.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (Shanghai Library seat booking) align with the code and files: CLI entrypoints, API client, Playwright-based login, and profile file storage. Required binaries (node/npm/npx) are appropriate; no unrelated cloud credentials or external services are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and scripts instruct the agent to run local Node scripts, optionally launch Playwright for manual browser login, and read/write profile JSON in ~/.config/shlibrary-seat-booking. All referenced files/paths and network calls correspond to the stated booking workflow. There are no instructions to scan unrelated system files or to exfiltrate data to unknown endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Install spec only recommends installing Node (brew formula for macOS/Linux). Runtime instructions call for `npm install` and `npx playwright install chromium`, which will download Playwright and a Chromium binary from Playwright's hosts — expected for browser automation but is a network download of an executable. The manifest contains two brew entries (darwin and linux) for the same formula; redundant but not harmful.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables or third-party credentials are requested. The skill stores and reads auth tokens (accessToken, sign, timestamp, optionally xEncode) from user-controlled profile files under ~/.config/shlibrary-seat-booking; this is necessary for the booking flow but means these files contain sensitive tokens and should be protected (file permissions suggested in docs).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill does not request permanent/always-on privilege. It reads and writes its own profile files in the user's home config directory (expected behavior). It does not modify other skills' configs or system-wide settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This repository appears to implement exactly what it claims: a local Node CLI that automates login (Playwright) and calls the Shanghai Library booking API. Before installing/running: 1) Inspect the login script (login.js / login_and_get_auth_node.js) to confirm it only opens a browser for manual login and saves tokens locally; 2) Be aware `npm install` + `npx playwright install chromium` will download packages and a Chromium binary from upstream servers — run these commands in an environment you trust; 3) Protect the profile files (~/.config/shlibrary-seat-booking/profiles/*.json) because they store accessToken/sign/timestamp; do not commit or share them; 4) The brew install entries are reasonable but redundant; you only need Node installed once. If you want extra caution, run the skill in an isolated VM/container or review the login code in detail to ensure it does not post your tokens to unexpected endpoints (the printed code only targets yuyue.library.sh.cn and related library hosts).
